items.q: Was WWI caused only by the assassination of Franz Ferdinand?
items.correct: No — that was the trigger; long-term causes included alliances, militarism, imperialism and nationalism.
items.misconception: Yes, that was the sole cause.
items.random_wrong: It was caused by the Treaty of Versailles.
items.why: The assassination sparked a crisis among already-tense, heavily-armed alliance systems.

items.q: What was fighting on the Western Front mostly like?
items.correct: Trench warfare and stalemate for long periods.
items.why: After 1914 the front settled into entrenched positions and attritional warfare.
